title: Last regular bands: Dickerson, Cook, Hines, WPA band and Zilner Randolph
summary: After Hines the Depression cut work; he played in Norman Black's WPA brass band and finally Zilner Randolph's dance band.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Uh-huh. What were your last jobs about? I didn't cover all of that last part of your life when you... Like after you'd made the records with Jolly Roll Martin, we talked quite a while about that. I wondered after that period which band you were with. You mentioned Hines. Uh-huh.

Oh, yes. Well... Dickerson, others. Well, now after that, let's see, Dickerson and Charlie Cook. Now, I worked with Charlie Cook several times. I've... See, I think I went back with Dickerson, and then was back with Charlie Cook. See, I've moved them on those jobs several times. And then, uh, let's see, where else was it? I can't think of who I worked with before I went with Earl. I think it was Charlie. After I left Charlie Cook, I went with Earl. And Earl is about the last band that is working regularly that I worked with. You worked regularly with. Uh-huh. Then things begin to get bad, and I used to work around. Yeah, the depression came along that time. Yeah. Bad for everybody. Uh-huh. Now, they just pick up little odd jobs then.
You were in the WPA band there for a while, wasn't it?

Yeah, yeah. I went to one rehearsal. I'm not sure if you were there or not. There's so many people there. Yeah, I was in that project band with, uh, with, uh, uh, Norman Black had the band. He was the leader. Yeah. Uh-huh. They had a pretty good band there, too. But, uh...
Was that more of a brass band or dance?
It was a brass band. That's what I thought.

Then, uh, then I worked with, uh, Randolph, too. He had a band on that. Oh, yes. Irving Randolph. Oh, Zildon. Oh, yes. He wrote Old Man Moe. Old Man Moe, that's right. Yeah. I worked with his band on that. He was on that. But he had a dance band.

Uh-huh. I worked with him on that. That was about the last, uh, the last, uh, uh, band that I worked with. But, uh, Zildon, he, uh, I don't know where he's still around here in Chicago, too. But I don't think he... I think he's...
I knew a few years ago, about seven years ago, I met him. He used to be at the Indiana Theater. Yeah, yeah, yeah. And he lived next door to Mahalia Jackson. I used to go to her house occasionally.
Yeah, yeah, yeah. And, uh, I'd hear him practicing and teaching next door to Mahalia. Yeah, that's what he's doing now. On the 3700 Prairie. That's right, that's right.
Yeah, yeah. Yeah, I think that's, that's what he's...
I haven't seen him for several years. But that's what he's doing, he's teaching. Yeah, he, that, that, those are the last outfits that, uh, that I, I worked with.
